subject: pathology
title: Non-Hodgkin lymphomas and chronic lymphoid leukaemias: key entities and markers

steps.tx: Non-Hodgkin lymphomas are mostly **B-cell** or **T-cell** neoplasms, and the grade of the tumour remains the main determinant of prognosis. High-grade lymphomas such as diffuse large B-cell lymphoma are potentially curable, while low-grade ones run an indolent course. Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is the most common aggressive subtype. Gastrointestinal tract is the commonest extranodal site, and the stomach accounts for about half of those cases.

steps.tx: Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia is the most common leukaemia of adults in the Western world, with a median age near 60. Diagnostic features include an absolute lymphocyte count above 5000 per cubic millimetre, **smudge cells** on the blood film, and co-expression of **CD5** and **CD23** along with pan-B markers CD19 and CD20. Proliferation centres are pathognomonic.

steps.tx: Translocations define several entities. **t(14;18)** places BCL2 next to the IGH locus in follicular lymphoma, blocking apoptosis. **t(11;14)** juxtaposes cyclin D1 with IGH in **mantle cell lymphoma**, which is CD5 positive and CD23 negative. **t(8;14)** moves **c-MYC** to IGH in Burkitt lymphoma, the commonest translocation in that disease at about 80 percent.

steps.tx: Burkitt lymphoma is a mature **germinal centre B-cell** tumour in children and young adults, with a high mitotic index. Macrophages clearing apoptotic debris give the **starry sky** pattern. It always lacks BCL2 protein, which distinguishes it from other germinal centre tumours. Endemic forms in Africa involve the jaw, and sporadic forms often involve the ileocaecal region.

steps.tx: Gastric MALT lymphoma is a B-cell tumour strongly linked to **H. pylori** infection, which is present in roughly 80 percent of cases. Antibiotic eradication can induce durable remission, so this is the first-line approach in early disease. Lymphoepithelial lesions are typical. Diagnosis is by endoscopic biopsy, and these tumours express CD19 and CD20 but not CD5, CD10 or CD23.

steps.tx: Mycosis fungoides and Sezary syndrome are cutaneous **T-cell lymphomas**, typically of CD4 positive helper T cells. Sezary syndrome shows **Sezary cells** in the blood, generalised lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly. Hairy cell leukaemia is a B-cell neoplasm with splenomegaly, pancytopenia and a tendency to atypical mycobacterial infection, and it is positive for TRAP.
